Team — forwarding Zenware's redlines. Key asks from their counsel summarized above. Quick questions:

1) Output ownership: can we accept a customer ownership model for Output (customer \"owns\" generated content) while preserving our ability to operate and improve the service (safety fixes, duplicate detection, abuse prevention)?
2) Training prohibition: is a clause that prohibits using Customer Content/Output to retrain models acceptable if we reserve the right to use de-identified, aggregated telemetry for safety and quality?
3) Feedback license: can we propose a narrowly tailored, non-exclusive license for aggregated telem/metrics only?

Karthik — can you draft suggested counter-language we can share with Zenware legal.
Sofia — any product/ops constraints (retention windows, logs, debugging) we need to call out?
Marcus — possible commercial tradeoffs (discounts/premium for opt-in training)?

I will draft an Order Form counter and attach here. Need greenlight to send to Melanie.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Zenware MSA & OF: redlines re: IP and training

Priyom — draft language below we can propose. I tried to be conservative for legal but leave product room to operate. Please review and flag anything that won't work operationally.

--- Proposed redline (Order Form / MSA language) ---
1) Output. \"Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Output generated by the Service using Customer Content. \"

2) Feedback & Service Improvement License. \"Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to use Feedback provided by Customer solely to operate, maintain and improve Redwood's services; such use shall be limited to aggregated, de-identified data and telemetry that cannot be reconstituted to identify Customer or Customer Content. Feedback shall not include Customer Content or Output used to train Redwood's base models without an explicit, separate opt-in in writing.\"

3) Training prohibition carveout. \"Redwood will not use Customer Content or Output to train or update its base models unless Customer provides an explicit opt-in. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use aggregated and de-identified usage metrics and synthetic examples derived from such metrics for internal safety testing and performance tuning, provided such materials cannot be traced back to Customer data.\"

--- End language ---

Notes: we should also add a short operational definition section for \"Feedback\" vs \"Telemetry\" vs \"Training\" to avoid ambiguity. If product needs short retention windows (eg 30 days for debugging) we can put that in an SOW or Order Form addendum.

If we send this, recommend attaching a marked-up order form with a checkbox option for customers to opt-in to model training (and corresponding commercial credit).

-Karthik
Legal / Head of Contracts (acting)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Zenware MSA & OF: redlines re: IP and training

Thanks Karthik — that wording aligns with what I was thinking. A few product/ops points to raise before we finalize: 

- Complete "Output ownership" without limits may restrict our ability to retain short excerpts needed to investigate abuse, debug regressions, or perform safety triage. Recommend explicit language permitting temporary retention of excerpts for debugging (e.g., up to 30 days) and a requirement that retained excerpts be encrypted and access-controlled.
- Aggregated/de-identified telemetry is fine, but we should define acceptable de-identification. Suggest a clause: \"De-identified means irreversible aggregation or hashing without keys that allow re-identification.\"
- For customers who opt-out of training, we should still be able to use anonymized failure traces for safety regression tests; propose explicit allowance for \"synthetic traces\" and safety-only tests.
- Product ask: add an \"Opt-in for model training\" option in the Order Form. Teams have asked for a commercial credit when customers opt to allow training. Marcus, can you weigh in on a pricing policy?

If legal is comfortable with the 30-day debugging retention + strict de-id language, I think this is a reasonable compromise that addresses Zenware's concerns while keeping our platform maintainable.

— Sofia
Product, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Zenware MSA & OF: redlines re: IP and training

Hi Melanie — thanks for the redlines. We've reviewed them internally and propose the following compromise to address Zenware's ownership/training concerns while allowing Redwood to operate and maintain service reliability and safety. Attached is a clean Order Form with the proposed language. Highlights below: 

- Output: we accept that the customer retains rights to Output.
- Training: Redwood will not use Customer Content or Output to train its base models unless Customer provides an explicit opt-in. We propose adding an \"Opt-in for model training\" checkbox in the Order Form. Customers who opt-in will receive a commercial credit; details are in the attached draft.
- Feedback/Telemetry: Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive license to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and Feedback solely to operate, maintain, and improve the Service. This expressly excludes using identifiable Customer Content or Output without opt-in.
- Short-term debugging retention: Redwood may retain transient excerpts of Content/Output for up to 30 days for abuse investigations, debugging, and safety triage; retained excerpts will be encrypted and access-controlled and not used to train models.

Please find the attached proposed-orderform-20270404.docx with the redline and a clean copy. If this looks acceptable in principle, can your counsel confirm the change to the training and telemetry clauses? We can then route a final marked copy for signature (we can support DocuSign).

Attachment: proposed-orderform-20270404.docx
Related: https://docusign.example/ZN-4783-sign

Thanks,
